s001.text: UPSC, twenty twenty-four. General Studies Paper Two, fifteen marks, two hundred and fifty words. Explain why privacy sits under Article twenty-one. Then discuss the law on a DNA test of a child in the womb, to prove paternity. Here is the strange part. We found no Supreme Court ruling on that second half.

s002.text: Read what it asks. Explain, then discuss. That is three jobs. Show why privacy sits in Article twenty-one. Give the law on paternity tests. Then deal with the child, and the womb.

s003.text: Start with the right. The word privacy is nowhere in the Constitution. In twenty seventeen, nine judges found it inside Article twenty-one. It is the core of human dignity.

s004.text: But the right is not absolute. A law must pass three tests. Legality, a legitimate aim, and proportionality. A court's order for a DNA test must pass the same kind of weighing.

s005.text: Now paternity. Section one-twelve of the Evidence Act says a child born in marriage is conclusively legitimate. Only proof of no access breaks it. The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam repeats it, in section one-sixteen.

s006.text: So courts are careful. In Goutam Kundu, no test as a matter of course. In Bhabani Prasad Jena, only on eminent need. In Dipanwita Roy, a test was allowed on a specific plea. And Firodia, in twenty twenty-three, refused it for a child.

s007.text: But all these cases concern a child already born. For the womb, the nearest law is the PC-PNDT Act. Section four allows pre-natal tests only for listed conditions. Paternity is not among them.

s008.text: Now we write. Two hundred and fifty words, about eleven minutes. Open with Puttaswamy and the clash it sets up. That one line frames the whole answer.

s009.text: Section one is the right: nine judges, dignity, and the three tests. Section two is the law on tests. Four cases and the section one-twelve presumption.

s010.text: Section three is the child. Use Firodia: legitimacy is part of a child's privacy. The child cannot be used as a pawn. Then state the limit honestly. We found no Supreme Court ruling on a foetal paternity test.

s011.text: Now the easy answer beside it. It says a husband can get a test whenever he doubts. Courts refuse that. It says pre-natal tests can settle paternity. The PC-PNDT Act does not allow that. It says privacy is absolute. It is not. And it says privacy is written in Article twenty-one. The word is not there.

s012.text: Here is the payoff. This answer serves its cousins. Twenty seventeen asked about the scope of Fundamental Rights after the privacy case. Twenty twenty-six asked about privacy and self-identity. Learn the three tests once.
